title: Eadro: An end-to-end troubleshooting framework for microservices on multi-source data
primary_claim: The results also show the usefulness of integrating multi-source data.
claim_quote: The results also show the usefulness of integrating multi-source data.
direct_endpoint: Anomaly detection and ranked root-cause microservice localization
endpoint_metric: Precision, recall, and F1 for anomaly detection; HR@1/3/5 and NDCG@3/5 for localization
validation_summary: Full Eadro is compared with task baselines and modality/graph ablations on both benchmark systems; removing traces or metrics materially reduces localization performance, while logs contribute less.
validation_quote: In conclusion, the involved data sources can all contribute to the effectiveness of Eadro to some degree, and traces contribute the most to the overall effectiveness.
validation_locator: PDF pp. 9-10, Section V-G (RQ3: Contributions of Different Data Sources), Table IV
disagreement_fields: intended_interpretation | plausible_alternative | endpoint_compatibility | discriminating_observation | assumptions | expected_under_claim | expected_under_alternative | status_basis
adjudicated_intended_interpretation: Integrating multiple data modalities (logs, KPIs, traces) within Eadro's end-to-end framework yields materially better anomaly detection and root-cause localization performance than single-modality input, reflecting genuine cross-modal complementarity where each modality contributes unique, non-substitutable diagnostic signal.
adjudicated_plausible_alternative: The observed multi-source performance gain is driven primarily by the single strongest modality (traces) plus differences in model capacity between the full multimodal model and its modality-drop ablations, rather than by genuine case-level cross-modal synergies among all three sources.
adjudicated_endpoint_compatibility: The reported modality-drop ablation in Table IV (Section V-G, RQ3) establishes that removing traces or KPIs reduces localization HR@1, HR@5, and F1 on both TrainTicket and SocialNetwork. However, both the cross-modal complementarity interpretation and the strong-single-modality-plus-capacity alternative are fully compatible with this result: genuine complementarity predicts performance drops when modalities are removed, but removing any informative features or reducing model capacity also predicts performance drops regardless of whether the modalities are complementary. The current design does not compare the full multimodal model against a capacity-matched single-modality variant, nor does it provide per-case evidence showing that different modalities contribute uniquely on different faults, so it cannot distinguish true cross-modal synergy from a dominant single modality carrying most of the load.
adjudicated_discriminating_observation: On the same TrainTicket and SocialNetwork benchmark cases and identical train/test splits, compare full three-modality Eadro against a single-modality traces-only variant in which the traces encoder is scaled up so that total parameter count, training budget, and the downstream GAT plus task heads remain architecturally matched; measure HR@1, HR@5, and F1 aggregated across datasets and broken down per fault case.
adjudicated_assumptions: (1) Parameter count and training budget can be meaningfully equalized across single- and multi-modal variants so that the comparison isolates data contribution rather than model capacity. (2) The traces-only variant can receive the same GAT-level service topology and task heads as the full model without structural change. (3) The benchmark fault distribution contains at least some faults that are invisible in traces but detectable in other modalities; otherwise complementarity is trivially untestable. (4) Per-case pairing holds the same faults and evaluation windows across conditions.
adjudicated_expected_under_claim: Full multimodal Eadro achieves substantially higher HR@1, HR@5, and F1 than the capacity-matched traces-only variant on both datasets, with gains spread across a majority of individual fault cases, indicating genuine complementary information from logs and KPIs beyond what traces alone can provide.
adjudicated_expected_under_alternative: Once parameter count and training budget are equalized, the traces-only variant achieves HR@1, HR@5, and F1 close to the full multimodal model on most individual cases, indicating that the apparent multi-source gain is mainly a capacity effect and dominance by the strongest modality rather than broad cross-modal complementarity.
adjudication_reason: Both reviewers independently identified the same alternative (strong modality plus capacity) and the same missing test (capacity-matched single-modality variant). Reviewer A's observation was slightly more case-level focused; Reviewer B's endpoint compatibility better articulated the three-part structure. The adjudicated version integrates the three-part endpoint compatibility (measured fact / joint compatibility / missing distinction) and an observation that clearly specifies the matched-capacity traces-only control, unit of analysis (per-case), metrics, and divergent expectations. | Status basis: Adjudication merges both reviewers' analysis: the paper already reports aggregate modality-drop ablations (Table IV) showing that removing traces or KPIs materially reduces performance, which is consistent with complementarity but does not isolate it. Missing are (1) a capacity-matched single-modality traces-only baseline that controls for total model size and training compute, and (2) a per-case breakdown showing case-level complementarity. The ablation is a necessary but not sufficient step. The existing-test status is PARTIAL.
validation_design_clarification: No wording change. The matched traces-only condition already specifies paired cases, capacity, training budget and downstream architecture.

title: Robust failure diagnosis of microservice system through multimodal data
primary_claim: combining these sources of data (multimodal data) leads to a more accurate diagnosis
claim_quote: In this study, we conduct an empirical study using real-world failure cases to show that combining these sources of data (multimodal data) leads to a more accurate diagnosis.
direct_endpoint: Root-cause instance localization and failure-type determination
endpoint_metric: A@1/A@3/A@5 and Avg@5 for localization; precision, recall, and F1 for failure type
datasets: D1: GAIA/MicroSS; D2: management system of a top-tier commercial bank
validation_summary: DiagFusion is compared against six single-modal and two multimodal baselines; component ablations test embedding, augmentation, GNN, and classifier choices.
validation_quote: DiagFusion outperforms existing methods in terms of root cause instance localization (improving by 20.9% to 368%) and failure type determination (improving by 11.0% to 169%).
validation_locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract; detailed results in Section 5.2
disagreement_fields: intended_interpretation | plausible_alternative | endpoint_compatibility | discriminating_observation | assumptions | expected_under_claim | expected_under_alternative | status_basis
adjudicated_intended_interpretation: Combining multiple failure data modalities (metrics, traces, logs) through DiagFusion's embedding-augmentation-GNN-classifier pipeline produces genuinely complementary diagnostic signals across modalities, and this cross-modal complementarity is the primary reason the method achieves higher root-cause localization and failure-type determination accuracy than single-modal approaches.
adjudicated_plausible_alternative: DiagFusion outperforms existing single-modal baselines mainly because of its stronger overall architecture design (embedding quality, data augmentation, graph modeling, classifier choices) rather than cross-modal complementarity per se; a well-designed single-modal model with the same architectural components and comparable capacity could achieve most of the observed accuracy gain.
adjudicated_endpoint_compatibility: The reported comparisons establish that DiagFusion outperforms six single-modal and two multimodal baselines on A@k/Avg@5 localization and failure-type P/R/F1 across D1 (GAIA/MicroSS) and D2 (commercial bank management system), and component ablations show that embedding, augmentation, GNN, and classifier each contribute. However, both the cross-modal complementarity interpretation and the architecture-strength alternative are fully compatible with these results: the single-modal baselines differ from DiagFusion in both modality count and method design, so a multimodal model with a superior architecture will naturally outperform simpler single-modal baselines regardless of whether cross-modal complementarity is the driver. The current design does not isolate the cross-modal contribution by holding the architecture fixed and varying only the input modality, so it cannot distinguish complementarity-driven gains from architecture-driven gains.
adjudicated_discriminating_observation: On the same D1 and D2 datasets and identical train/test splits, compare full multimodal DiagFusion against a set of matched single-modal variants (metrics-only, traces-only, logs-only) that reuse DiagFusion's exact embedding module, same augmentation strategy, same GNN graph modeling, and same classifier, with only the input modality changed and total model capacity matched across conditions; measure A@1/A@3/A@5 and Avg@5 for localization and precision/recall/F1 for failure type.
adjudicated_assumptions: (1) The embedding, GNN, and classifier components can be meaningfully applied to single-modal input while keeping total parameter count and training budget comparable to the full model. (2) The six existing single-modal baselines use different architectures and therefore confound modality count with method quality, motivating the matched-architecture comparison. (3) Per-fault-type analysis can further differentiate which gains come from modality-specific faults versus general architectural advantage.
adjudicated_expected_under_claim: Full multimodal DiagFusion significantly outperforms every architecture-matched single-modal variant on both datasets across A@1, A@5, Avg@5, and failure-type F1, demonstrating that cross-modal complementarity contributes substantially beyond the architectural components alone.
adjudicated_expected_under_alternative: The best architecture-matched single-modal variant achieves performance close to full DiagFusion, closing most of the gap between the existing simpler single-modal baselines and the multimodal model, meaning that most of DiagFusion's advantage comes from better architecture rather than cross-modal complementarity.
adjudication_reason: Both reviewers converged on the same alternative (architecture strength) and the same missing test (architecture-matched single-modal variants). Reviewer B's endpoint compatibility more precisely articulated the three-part structure. Both reviewers' existing-test status was PARTIAL, which is retained. | Status basis: The paper compares DiagFusion against six single-modal and two multimodal baselines and reports component ablations (embedding, augmentation, GNN, classifier). This shows that each component contributes and that multimodal input helps, but it does not cleanly separate cross-modal complementarity from architectural superiority because the single-modal baselines use entirely different methods. Missing are architecture-matched single-modal variants of DiagFusion itself with comparable capacity, which would directly isolate the cross-modal contribution. The existing-test status is PARTIAL.
validation_design_clarification: No wording change. Keep the shared architecture, capacity and train/test splits in the detailed record.

title: No More Data Silos: Unified Microservice Failure Diagnosis with Temporal Knowledge Graph
primary_claim: represent the state of systems comprehensively
claim_quote: UniDiag applies a simple yet effective stream-based anomaly detection method to reduce computational cost and a novel microservice-oriented graph embedding method to represent the state of systems comprehensively.
endpoint_metric: Weighted-average precision, recall, and F1; NMI and ACC for embedding/cluster ablations
datasets: D1: GAIA/MicroSS; D2: simulated e-commerce microservice application
validation_summary: The evaluation reports classification outcomes, component ablations, modality-drop ablations, new-failure tests, and embedding NMI/ACC on two datasets.
validation_quote: In conclusion, integrating all three data modalities significantly enhances UniDiag's effectiveness, highlighting the crucial role of diverse data in improving failure diagnosis.
validation_locator: PDF p. 10, Section V-D (RQ3) and Table VI
disagreement_fields: intended_interpretation | plausible_alternative | endpoint_compatibility | discriminating_observation | assumptions | expected_under_claim | expected_under_alternative | status_basis
adjudicated_intended_interpretation: UniDiag's temporal knowledge-graph representation comprehensively captures the state of microservice systems across data modalities, meaning the learned embedding encodes enough information about system structure and dynamics to reliably support a range of distinct downstream diagnostic tasks, not just the failure-type classification it is trained on.
adjudicated_plausible_alternative: UniDiag's representation is tuned specifically for failure-type classification on the tested datasets; its apparent comprehensiveness is a consequence of optimizing features for that one downstream task and its labels, and it may not generalize to other diagnostic tasks or unrelated system-state queries.
adjudicated_endpoint_compatibility: The reported evaluation establishes that UniDiag achieves strong weighted precision, recall, and F1 on failure-type classification, and its embedding/cluster analysis shows high NMI and ACC when clusters are aligned against failure-type labels, across both D1 (GAIA/MicroSS) and D2 (simulated e-commerce microservice). However, both the comprehensive-system-state interpretation and the task-tuned-representation alternative are fully compatible with these results: a representation optimized for one specific task can achieve high classification accuracy and cluster alignment with that task's labels without being broadly comprehensive of system state. The current design does not evaluate the representation on any downstream task or criterion independent of failure-type classification labels, so it cannot distinguish a representation that captures broad system state from one specialized for the evaluated diagnostic task.
adjudicated_discriminating_observation: On the same D1 and D2 datasets, take the frozen UniDiag temporal knowledge-graph representation and evaluate it on a set of auxiliary tasks that are meaningful but unrelated to failure-type classification (e.g., near-future service resource utilization prediction, held-out modality reconstruction from the representation of other modalities, or propagation subgraph recovery) using linear probes or light fine-tuning under a fixed training budget; compare against a task-agnostic baseline representation of the same dimension. Prespecify a task-agnostic baseline trained on the same input, with the same representation dimension; compare frozen encoders using the same probe architecture, training data and budget across auxiliary tasks.
adjudicated_assumptions: (1) Suitable auxiliary tasks exist that measure system-state comprehensiveness independently of failure-type labels and whose ground truth (e.g., resource utilization windows) is available in the same datasets. (2) The representation is frozen across tasks (linear probe or light fine-tuning) so that the comparison isolates representation quality rather than task-specific architecture. (3) Representation dimension and data splits are held constant across comparison conditions. | Independent-validation clarification: Prespecify a task-agnostic baseline trained on the same input, with the same representation dimension; compare frozen encoders using the same probe architecture, training data and budget across auxiliary tasks.
adjudicated_expected_under_claim: The frozen UniDiag temporal knowledge-graph representation yields strong performance across multiple distinct auxiliary system-state prediction tasks relative to dimension-matched task-agnostic baselines, in addition to strong failure-type classification, indicating that the representation captures genuinely broad system state rather than task-specific features.
adjudicated_expected_under_alternative: The UniDiag representation achieves strong performance on failure-type classification but shows little to no consistent advantage over task-agnostic baselines on auxiliary system-state prediction tasks, indicating that the representation is specialized for the classification task rather than comprehensively encoding system state.
adjudication_reason: Both reviewers converged on the same alternative (task-tuned representation) and the same NO status. Reviewer B's auxiliary-task formulation (resource utilization prediction, held-out modality reconstruction) is more concrete than Reviewer A's and is retained. | Status basis: The paper evaluates the representation only through failure-type classification (weighted P/R/F1), modality-drop ablations, new-failure tests, and NMI/ACC clustering analysis. All of these evaluate the representation in the context of the same diagnostic task and its labels; the NMI/ACC analysis uses failure-type labels and is therefore consistent with both interpretations. title: TVDiag: A Task-oriented and View-invariant Failure Diagnosis Framework for Microservice-based Systems with Multimodal Data
primary_claim: TVDiag targets view-invariant failure diagnosis across multimodal data.
claim_quote: TVDiag employs task-oriented learning to enhance the potential advantages of each modality and establishes cross-modal associations based on contrastive learning to extract view-invariant failure information.
direct_endpoint: Ranked root-cause localization and failure-type identification
endpoint_metric: HR@1, HR@3, and Avg@3 for localization; precision, recall, and F1 for type identification
endpoint_target: Root-cause microservice instance and failure type
datasets: A: GAIA/MicroSS; B: AIOps-22; C: Sock Shop with Chaos Mesh fault injection
validation_summary: Task, cross-modal, graph-augmentation, and dynamic-weight modules are ablated; the cross-modal module is assessed through downstream localization and type-identification endpoints.
validation_quote: TVDiag outperforms TVDiag w/o CM on HR@1 and F1-score across two datasets, owing to the preservation of view-invariant information.
disagreement_fields: intended_interpretation | plausible_alternative | endpoint_compatibility | discriminating_observation | assumptions | expected_under_claim | expected_under_alternative | status_basis
adjudicated_intended_interpretation: TVDiag's cross-modal (CM) contrastive learning module extracts failure information that is invariant to which modality (view) provides the evidence, so the same failure state is recognized similarly regardless of which sensor modality is dominant or available at test time.
adjudicated_plausible_alternative: The CM module improves downstream performance primarily through general regularization and representation-enrichment effects (similar to auxiliary losses or multi-task learning) rather than by extracting genuinely view-invariant features; performance improvements do not imply that the same fault is recognizable when the modality view is switched.
adjudicated_endpoint_compatibility: The reported CM-module ablation in Section 5.3 (RQ2, Table 6) establishes that removing the cross-modal module reduces HR@1 and F1 on the GAIA and AIOps-22 datasets, which the paper attributes to preservation of view-invariant information. However, both the view-invariance interpretation and the general-regularization alternative are fully compatible with this result: any well-designed auxiliary loss or cross-modal constraint can improve downstream performance through regularization or representation enrichment alone, without the representation being genuinely invariant across modality views. The current design only measures downstream endpoint changes from adding or removing the CM module, and does not directly test whether the learned representation can recognize the same fault when the input modality view is switched, so it cannot distinguish view-invariant feature extraction from general regularization benefits. View invariance must not be expanded to cross-organization, cross-version, or arbitrary production generalization.
adjudicated_discriminating_observation: On the same datasets (A: GAIA/MicroSS, B: AIOps-22, C: Sock Shop), train a diagnostic head on the frozen TVDiag-CM representation using only one modality view (e.g., metrics) at training time, then test performance when the input is switched to a different modality view (e.g., traces) of the same fault instances; compare the cross-modal transfer accuracy of TVDiag-with-CM against (a) TVDiag-without-CM and (b) a variant where the CM loss is replaced by a comparable-capacity generic regularization (e.g., within-modality masked reconstruction).
adjudicated_assumptions: (1) Fault instances have aligned representations across modalities so that cross-modal transfer can be meaningfully tested. (2) The diagnostic head can be cleanly separated from the representation encoder. (3) The amount and form of regularization from the CM loss can be approximated by alternative regularization schemes for fair comparison of total capacity. (4) All other modules (task-oriented learning, graph augmentation, dynamic weighting) are held constant across conditions.
adjudicated_expected_under_claim: TVDiag with the CM module achieves substantially higher cross-modal transfer accuracy (recognizing the same fault from a different modality view at test time) than both TVDiag without CM and a regularization-matched baseline, demonstrating that the CM module extracts genuinely view-invariant failure information rather than providing only generic regularization.
adjudicated_expected_under_alternative: TVDiag with CM shows cross-modal transfer performance comparable to the regularization-matched baseline, indicating that the CM module benefit comes from general regularization effects rather than from true view-invariant feature extraction; view-switch test scenarios show no specific robustness advantage for CM.
adjudication_reason: Both reviewers identified the same alternative (general regularization) and the same PARTIAL status. Reviewer B's cross-modal transfer test design is more precise (train on one view, test on another) and forms the backbone of the adjudicated observation. | Status basis: The paper reports a CM ablation in Section 5.3 (RQ2) showing that removing CM reduces HR@1 and F1, and it interprets this as evidence of view-invariant information preservation. The ablation is necessary for the claim but not sufficient: it shows the CM module helps downstream performance, but it does not directly test view-invariance (the ability to recognize the same fault across different modality views). Missing are (1) a cross-modal transfer or modality-switch evaluation that directly tests whether the representation is invariant across views, and (2) a capacity-matched generic-regularization control. The existing-test status is PARTIAL.
validation_design_clarification: No wording change. The matched control and same-fault view switch are explicit in the detailed record.

title: CloudRCA: A root cause analysis framework for cloud computing platforms
primary_claim: performs more robustly with respect to algorithmic configurations
claim_quote: CloudRCA ... performs more robustly with respect to algorithmic configurations.
endpoint_metric: Macro precision, cover rate, F1, and running time
datasets: Alibaba MaxCompute, Realtime Compute, and Hologres
validation_summary: CloudRCA is evaluated across three production platforms, with parameter sweeps and comparisons to alternative RCA methods plus cross-platform transfer experiments.
validation_quote: KHBN also seems to perform less sensitively with respect to the parameters, and thus can deliver a more stable performance in practice.
disagreement_fields: intended_interpretation | plausible_alternative | endpoint_compatibility | discriminating_observation | assumptions | expected_under_claim | expected_under_alternative | status_basis
adjudicated_intended_interpretation: CloudRCA's core KHBN component is robust to changes in its own algorithmic configuration parameters — specifically significance level α, max_num_of_leaf, and distance threshold θ — meaning root-cause type inference performance remains stable across a meaningful range of parameter settings, making it reliable in practice without careful tuning.
adjudicated_plausible_alternative: KHBN appears robust only within the narrow range of significance level α, max_num_of_leaf, and distance threshold θ actually tested on MaxCompute in Section 4.5; beyond that range performance degrades sharply, and the apparent robustness reflects a favorable choice of tested parameter region rather than an inherent property of the algorithm.
adjudicated_endpoint_compatibility: The reported parameter-sensitivity analysis in Section 4.5, conducted exclusively on Alibaba MaxCompute, establishes that KHBN performance varies less with changes to significance level α, max_num_of_leaf, and distance threshold θ than the compared methods within the tested ranges. However, both the genuine algorithmic-configuration-robustness interpretation and the narrow-favorable-range alternative are fully compatible with this result: a method that is only stable within a certain parameter window will still look robust if the sweep stays within that window, and the tested ranges are not shown to be wide or stressful. The three-platform experiments (MaxCompute, Realtime Compute, Hologres) and cross-platform transfer results evaluate a separate claim about distribution-shift/deployment robustness and must not be conflated with algorithmic-configuration robustness. The current design does not extend the sweep to substantially wider ranges of α, max_num_of_leaf, and θ on MaxCompute, nor does it quantify worst-case performance drops across a broader parameter space, so it cannot distinguish inherent robustness from a fortunate choice of test region.
adjudicated_discriminating_observation: On MaxCompute (the same platform used for Section 4.5), extend the parameter sweep for KHBN and each comparison method to a substantially wider range of settings for the three formal parameters — significance level α, max_num_of_leaf, and distance threshold θ — including values that deviate far from defaults in both directions (very small and very large α, very small and very large max_num_of_leaf, very small and very large θ); measure macro precision, cover rate, and F1 across all settings; compute coefficient of variation (std/mean) and worst-case performance drop from the best configuration for each method. Freeze an operationally feasible expanded parameter envelope before inspection of results; report non-functional settings separately and calculate variability and worst-case degradation within feasible settings for each method.
adjudicated_assumptions: (1) A wider parameter range is computationally feasible, and degenerate/extreme settings for α, max_num_of_leaf, and θ can be defined a priori without cherry-picking. (2) Performance metrics (macro precision, cover rate, F1) can be consistently computed across all settings. (3) Algorithmic-configuration robustness (robustness to the algorithm's own hyperparameters) is kept distinct from cross-platform transfer robustness, with the test conducted on MaxCompute only as in Section 4.5. | Independent-validation clarification: Freeze an operationally feasible expanded parameter envelope before inspection of results; report non-functional settings separately and calculate variability and worst-case degradation within feasible settings for each method.
adjudicated_expected_under_claim: Across a substantially wider range of significance level α, max_num_of_leaf, and distance threshold θ on MaxCompute, KHBN maintains substantially lower coefficient of variation in macro precision, cover rate, and F1 than comparison methods, with a smaller worst-case drop from the best configuration, confirming genuine algorithmic-configuration robustness rather than stability within a narrow tested band.
adjudicated_expected_under_alternative: When parameter ranges are expanded beyond the Section 4.5 tested settings, KHBN's macro precision, cover rate, and F1 vary substantially (coefficient of variation comparable to or higher than baselines) with large worst-case drops, showing that its apparent robustness is an artifact of a narrow tested parameter region.
adjudication_reason: Both reviewers converged on the three correct formal parameters (α, max_num_of_leaf, θ) and the MaxCompute-only restriction, removing the erroneous parameters present in earlier revisions. Reviewer B more carefully separated algorithmic-configuration robustness from distribution-shift/cross-platform robustness, which is retained in the adjudicated version. Both reviewers rated PARTIAL. | Status basis: Section 4.5 reports parameter sensitivity experiments on MaxCompute varying α, max_num_of_leaf, and θ and concludes that KHBN is less sensitive to parameters. Three production platforms are separately evaluated for cross-platform transfer, which is a different construct. The Section 4.5 sweep is a relevant start but does not establish that the tested ranges are broad enough; missing is an extended parameter sweep covering a much wider range for the three formal parameters on MaxCompute, with quantitative robustness metrics (coefficient of variation, worst-case drop) compared across methods. The existing-test status is PARTIAL.
factual_source_locator: C049.pdf Section 4.5, PDF p. 8; the three formal parameters are significance level α, max_num_of_leaf, distance threshold θ.
validated_table3_claim: Diagnosis is robust to configuration changes
validation_design_clarification: Clarify the detailed observation: freeze an operationally feasible range before results, report non-functional settings separately, and calculate variability and worst-case degradation within the feasible range for each compared method. The Table 3 summary remains unchanged.

title: Generic and Robust Performance Diagnosis via Causal Inference for OLTP Database Systems
primary_claim: CauseRank presents generic and robust database performance diagnosis.
claim_quote: The core idea and framework of CauseRank are generic and can be applied to other large-scale system components.
direct_endpoint: Ranking of root-cause infrastructure metric groups
endpoint_metric: Top-k accuracy A@1/A@3/A@5, mean average rank (MAR), and localization time
datasets: 97 real-world failures of 9 types from a production Oracle database in a large commercial bank; 233 infrastructure metrics grouped into 26 groups
validation_summary: CauseRank is compared with four baselines on one production Oracle database; variants remove domain knowledge, and parameter-sensitivity experiments vary graph/ranking settings.
validation_quote: Results show that CauseRank ranks the root causes at top-5 for 93.8%, top-3 for 82.5% of all the failures, with an average localization time of 12.58 seconds per failure.
validation_locator: PDF p. 2, Introduction; Table II on PDF p. 7
disagreement_fields: intended_interpretation | plausible_alternative | endpoint_compatibility | discriminating_observation | assumptions | expected_under_claim | expected_under_alternative | status_basis
adjudicated_intended_interpretation: CauseRank presents its core causal-inference framework as applicable to other large-scale system components. Transfer with the core graph-construction and ranking methods unchanged is a proposed implication to test, not an empirical result established by its Oracle evaluation.
adjudicated_plausible_alternative: CauseRank works well on the tested Oracle database environment because its causal graph construction, metric grouping, and ranking heuristics are tailored to Oracle OLTP characteristics; its genericity is conceptual rather than empirically demonstrated, and applying it to substantially different system components would require significant adaptation or yield degraded performance.
adjudicated_endpoint_compatibility: The reported evaluation on 97 real-world failures from one production Oracle database (Table II) establishes that CauseRank achieves A@1/A@3/A@5 of 46.4%/73.2%/93.8% with a mean average rank of 2.13, outperforming four baselines in that environment; parameter-sensitivity experiments show stable performance across graph and ranking settings within this same Oracle environment. However, both the generic-framework interpretation and the environment-specific alternative are fully compatible with these results: a method optimized for one environment will show strong in-environment performance and within-environment parameter stability regardless of whether it generalizes to other system components. The current design does not include any evaluation on a different system component or database type with the same core framework and comparable ranking evaluation, so it cannot distinguish genuine cross-system generality from Oracle-specific effectiveness. Within-Oracle parameter sensitivity must not be treated as cross-system genericity evidence.
adjudicated_discriminating_observation: Apply the same CauseRank framework (with core causal-inference and ranking components unchanged, allowing only minimal schema-level adaptation such as mapping metric names) to at least one additional large-scale system component type with known ground-truth failures (e.g., a different database system, a distributed storage system, a message queue, or a cache layer); measure A@1/A@3/A@5 and MAR on that new system and compare CauseRank's performance against domain-specific baselines selected to be comparable to the four baselines used in the Oracle evaluation.
adjudicated_assumptions: (1) A suitable second system component is available with known ground-truth root-cause metric groups and a comparable volume of failures. (2) Only minimal schema-level adaptation is allowed; core causal graph construction and ranking algorithms remain unchanged. (3) Baselines for the new system are selected to be comparable in methodology to the four baselines in the Oracle evaluation, providing a fair relative comparison.
adjudicated_expected_under_claim: CauseRank achieves comparable top-k accuracy (A@1/A@3/A@5) and MAR advantages over domain-specific baselines on the second system component as it does on the Oracle database, demonstrating that the core framework is genuinely generic across different large-scale system components with only minimal input adaptation.
adjudicated_expected_under_alternative: CauseRank's performance advantage over baselines is substantially smaller or absent on the second system component compared to Oracle, or it requires major redesign of causal graph construction or ranking logic to work, indicating that its strong Oracle results are environment-specific rather than evidence of generic methodology.
adjudication_reason: Both reviewers converged on the same alternative (Oracle-specific effectiveness) and NO status. Reviewer B's formulation of the expected cross-system test is retained. | Status basis: The paper evaluates CauseRank exclusively on 97 real-world failures from one production Oracle database at a commercial bank. It reports comparisons with four baselines, domain-knowledge ablation variants, and parameter-sensitivity experiments, all within the same Oracle environment. While parameter sensitivity shows within-environment robustness, this does not address the cross-system genericity claim. Missing is any evaluation on a different system component or database type that would test whether the framework transfers. The existing-test status is NO.
factual_source_locator: C016.pdf Table II, PDF p. 7; all 97 failures come from one production Oracle database.
validated_table3_claim: Core framework can apply to other system components
validation_design_clarification: Revise the Table 3 scientific-claim cell from an achieved cross-system property to the paper's proposed applicability. Align Appendix F and the validated case record. Preserve the alternative and transfer observation; do not count this as independent support for the original claim wording.

adjudicated_intended_interpretation: Ungrounded diagnoses reflect deficits in causal-process reasoning: an agent can name a correct root-cause service yet fail to produce a causally correct propagation account. Outcome-only scoring hides this failure mode, while the case-level contrast tests whether ungrounded cases contain causal errors or omissions in the textual diagnosis or instead a correct textual account whose graph serialization breaks the required path.
adjudicated_plausible_alternative: The AnySvc-to-PR gap is primarily an artifact of graph-prediction quality issues that break the required directed path — specifically missing edges along the propagation chain, incorrect edge direction, or missing intermediate service nodes — rather than errors in the textual causal account. Crucially, extra or spurious edges in the predicted graph do not cause PR failure, because PR (Equation 10) requires only existence of at least one directed path from a correct root service to a ground-truth alarm node when AnySvc=1; the text may state the correct causal chain while missing connections or wrong directions prevent that path from existing in the graph.

Per PR definition (Appendix G.2.3, Equation 10), PR fails only when, given AnySvc=1, no directed path exists in the predicted graph from any correct root-cause service to any ground-truth alarm node; extra or spurious edges do not by themselves cause PR failure because the existence of one valid path is sufficient. However, both an explanation-level failure and the structural-path-breakage alternative are fully compatible with the 14.5-point gap: the textual diagnosis may contain causal errors or omit the propagation path, or it may state the correct account while missing edges, reversed directions, or missing intermediate nodes prevent a complete directed path from existing in the graph. The current design reports aggregate Node F1 and Edge F1, but these set-overlap metrics do not include a case-level decomposition of textual causal correctness versus graph-structural path breakage, so it cannot distinguish the two observable patterns.

Use a prespecified rubric for textual causal correctness versus structural graph-path breakage; obtain two independent blind expert labels per case, report raw agreement, and document resolution of disagreements.

(2) Evaluators are blinded to PR outcome, agent identity, and study hypothesis. (3) Sufficient case-level detail (text explanation plus graph structure) is available for judgment. (4) Cases where the graph contains extra spurious edges but also a correct directed path already score PR=1 and are correctly excluded from the ungrounded set. | Independent-validation clarification: Use a prespecified rubric for textual causal correctness versus structural graph-path breakage; obtain two independent blind expert labels per case, report raw agreement, and document resolution of disagreements.

Both reviewers rated PARTIAL. | Status basis: The paper reports AnySvc, PR, Node F1, and Edge F1 for 11 LLM backbones across 500 instances and three systems. endpoint_metric: AIOps2025: localization accuracy, type accuracy, strict evidence match, and response length; RCA100: Entity, Fault, and Process scores

datasets: AIOps2025 (400 cases) and RCA100 (103 cases), spanning HipsterShop and OpenTelemetry Demo Store environments

validation_quote: The Reason pillar is captured by a process score jointly measured by causal-chain node match rate and observability-checkpoint hit rate, so an agent must walk the right chain and cite the right evidence at each step.
disagreement_fields: intended_interpretation | plausible_alternative | endpoint_compatibility | discriminating_observation | assumptions | expected_under_claim | expected_under_alternative | status_basis
adjudicated_intended_interpretation: The Reason/Process dimension of the C090 benchmark genuinely measures the quality of an agent's diagnostic reasoning process — agents with higher Process scores (combining causal-chain node match rate and observability-checkpoint hit rate) are producing substantively better-reasoned diagnoses that would be judged more sound by human domain experts.
adjudicated_plausible_alternative: The Process score primarily measures how well an agent's output format matches the benchmark's expected structure (mentioning the right chain nodes and checkpoints in the expected template), but it does not strongly reflect the actual quality of reasoning as judged by human experts; an agent could achieve a high Process score by pattern-matching to expected structure without genuine diagnostic understanding.
adjudicated_endpoint_compatibility: The reported Process score, composed of causal-chain node match rate and observability-checkpoint hit rate, establishes that the benchmark can score agent outputs along a Reason dimension and that scores vary across agent backbones on AIOps2025 (400 cases) and RCA100 (103 cases). However, both the genuine-reasoning-quality interpretation and the output-format-matching alternative are fully compatible with these results: outputs that reflect better underlying reasoning may achieve higher chain-node and checkpoint scores, but outputs that merely match the expected structural template or keyword pattern without genuine reasoning depth can also score well. The current design does not include any independent human-expert assessment of reasoning quality against which the Process score could be validated, so it cannot distinguish whether the score measures genuine reasoning depth or primarily structural/format alignment with the benchmark rubric.
adjudicated_discriminating_observation: On a stratified sample of agent outputs from AIOps2025 and RCA100 covering a range of Process scores, have multiple blind human domain experts independently rate each agent output's diagnostic reasoning quality along a structured rubric (soundness of causal inference, appropriate use of evidence, correctness of intermediate steps, awareness of alternative explanations) without access to Process scores, benchmark node/checkpoint definitions, or agent identities; compute inter-rater reliability and then the rank/association between (blind) aggregated human reasoning-quality ratings and the automated Process scores across the sampled outputs.
adjudicated_assumptions: (1) Human experts with microservice failure diagnosis domain knowledge can reliably rate reasoning quality using a validated rubric. (2) Evaluators are properly blinded to Process scores, agent identity, and benchmark scoring criteria to avoid anchoring bias. (3) Inter-rater reliability reaches acceptable levels. (4) The sample covers a sufficient range of Process scores and agent backbones to make the association analysis meaningful.
adjudicated_expected_under_claim: The automated Process score shows a strong positive association with blind human expert ratings of diagnostic reasoning quality, with relatively few discordant cases (high Process score accompanied by low human-rated reasoning quality, or vice versa), confirming that the Reason dimension genuinely measures reasoning process quality rather than just structural format matching.
adjudicated_expected_under_alternative: The automated Process score shows only a weak association with blind human expert ratings of reasoning quality, with frequent discordant cases where high-scoring outputs receive low expert ratings and low-scoring outputs receive high expert ratings, indicating that the metric primarily measures how well output structure matches the expected format rather than substantive reasoning quality.
adjudication_reason: Both reviewers converged on the same alternative (format matching) and NO status. The paper validates the benchmark through competition participation and expert-labeled ground truth for entities/faults/chains/checkpoints. endpoint_metric: A@1/A@3/A@5, Avg@5, and online localization time
datasets: D1: simulated e-commerce system (46 instances); D2: top-tier commercial-bank management system/AIOps Challenge 2022 (18 instances)

adjudicated_plausible_alternative: DeepHunt's 'interpretability' consists of having decomposable internal components (reconstruction error term, propagation-pattern term, learned weights W1/W2, heatmaps) that can be inspected, but these inspectable internals do not necessarily improve human understanding or decision-making; the interpretability claim is about the model having a decomposable scoring structure rather than about being usefully interpretable to humans in practice.

adjudicated_expected_under_alternative: Participants using DeepHunt's interpretable output show no meaningful improvement in root-cause identification accuracy, diagnosis time, or confidence calibration compared with participants using a black-box ranked list of equal accuracy, indicating that the decomposable internals do not translate to useful human interpretability.

title: Can LLMs Really Recover Microservice Failures? A Recovery-Aware Evaluation of Diagnosis-to-Action Reasoning

endpoint_metric: RCA-Service/RCA-Type accuracy; Action Hit, Target Hit, Exact Match, Recovery Validity, and live Replay RV
endpoint_target: Root-cause service/type and incident-specific operation-target recovery plan
datasets: 302 quality-audited Kubernetes incidents from Online Boutique, six service roles and eight fault categories
validation_summary: All 302 incidents are replayed for Qwen-RAG after reinjecting the original fault and executing the predicted action. The reported recovery outcome is validity-gated: offline validity and restored health are both required.

adjudicated_plausible_alternative: The diagnosis-to-recovery gap may be inflated by the strict offline recovery-validity criteria: some offline-invalid predicted plans may have restored service health in the reported full live replay, but the validity-gated recovery count does not disclose those outcomes. If so, the gate would make practical recovery appear worse than the ungated live health result.
adjudicated_endpoint_compatibility: Table VIII (Section VI-E, RQ5) establishes that, out of 302 Qwen-RAG predicted plans across Online Boutique Kubernetes incidents, 146 are offline-valid and 146 are validity-gated live recoveries (i.e., offline-valid AND service health is restored after live replay), giving a validity-gated overall recovery rate of 146/302 = 48.3% across all 302 incidents, alongside offline Recovery Validity ranging from 36.8%–60.3% across models. The paper does not separately report live replay outcomes for plans that fail offline validity: live replay is executed for all 302 incidents but the recovered count is validity-gated, meaning a plan is counted as recovered only if it is offline-valid AND restores health. However, both the genuine plan-effectiveness-gap interpretation and the over-strict-offline-gate alternative are fully compatible with this overall 48.3% rate: a real gap in plan quality would produce a low gated recovery rate, but an offline-validity criterion that rejects many plans that would actually succeed in live replay would also produce a low gated overall rate. The current design does not separately report or compare live recovery outcomes broken down by offline validity group, so it does not observe whether offline-invalid plans would actually restore service in live replay; without this comparison it cannot determine whether the validity gate is appropriately calibrated or overly restrictive.
adjudicated_discriminating_observation: Using case-level outcomes from the reported full 302-incident Qwen-RAG live replay, report actual service-health restoration separately for offline-valid and offline-invalid predicted plans under the same fault-reinjection procedure and 75-second health window. Compare the ungated live recovery rate across all 302 incidents with the published validity-gated rate. If case-level live outcomes were not retained, repeat the same full replay while recording offline-validity and restored-health status for every incident.
adjudicated_assumptions: Case-level health outcomes are retained for every replayed plan, or the full replay can be repeated; offline-validity labels are fixed independently of the re-tabulation; the same 75-second health-restoration rule and fault reinjection procedure apply to both validity groups.
adjudicated_expected_under_claim: Offline-invalid plans show a substantially lower live recovery rate than offline-valid plans. This result would limit the strict-gate explanation while remaining consistent with a diagnosis-to-plan deficit; it would not by itself locate every source of recovery failure.
adjudicated_expected_under_alternative: Offline-invalid plans achieve a live recovery rate comparable to that of offline-valid plans. This result would show that the validity-gated 48.3% statistic omits successful recoveries and would support the strict-gate explanation.
adjudication_reason: Both reviewers converged on the same alternative (overly strict offline validity gate) and PARTIAL status. Reviewer B more precisely stated the denominator: 48.3% is 146/302 validity-gated overall rate (not offline-valid group rate), and that live replay is executed for all 302 but recovered counts are validity-gated. This is retained.
